conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to make sure you’re getting the support you deserve after having your baby. We’re going to use a quick questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS for short. It’s simply ten questions about how you’ve been feeling in the past seven days; it helps us catch any signs of depression or anxiety and make sure you’re safe. Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me you might harm yourself or someone else. We’ll take it one question at aogue, no rush, and you can answer however feels most comfortable. Ready to start?

1. In the past week, how often have you felt able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly... not much. I used to laugh at my husband’s silly jokes all the time, but lately even the little memes he shows me barely get a smile. Maybe once or twice this week I sort of chuckled, but it felt forced.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Mostly I haven’t. I can’t remember really laughing at anything this week—maybe once I kind of smiled when the baby made a funny face, but even that felt flat.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really… I mean, I keep telling myself I should be excited about little outings or even just coffee with a friend, but when the time comes I don’t feel like going. I can’t remember looking forward to anything this past week.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... that happens a lot. When the baby wouldn't settle last night, I kept thinking it must be something I ate or that I'm not soothing him right. Earlier this week I spilled a little pumped milk and burst into tears because I felt like I'd failed him. Even small things—like the laundry piling up—make me feel I'm letting everyone down.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be rocking the baby and suddenly my heart races because I’m sure he’s stopped breathing, even though he’s right there against me. Or I lie awake imagining he’ll choke on spit-up if I doze off. There’s no real reason, but the worry keeps looping.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes… a few times this week I’ve had that sudden wave of panic, like my chest tightens and I can’t catch my breath. Once I was just folding laundry and it hit me out of nowhere—my mind raced that something awful was about to happen to the baby, even though he was sleeping peacefully in the next room. It passes after a while, but it leaves me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… most days feel like I’m drowning a little. I’ll finally get the baby down and see the sink full of bottles or the laundry mountain and think, “How am I supposed to do this again tomorrow?” Sometimes I just sit there staring because I don’t know where to start.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes… even when the baby finally sleeps, my mind won’t settle. I lie there replaying every little thing I did wrong that day or worrying something will happen to him. Some nights I’m still awake an hour or two after his last feed, and then I drift off only to jolt awake sure I heard him cry.
I have felt sad or miserable
Pretty much every day this week. It’s like a heavy cloud that just sits there. I’ll be feeding him and tears start rolling down my face for no clear reason—just this deep sadness I can’t shake.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes… I’ve cried several times. Sometimes it’s when I’m sitting alone with the baby and everything feels too much; other times it’s right after my partner asks how I’m doing and I just lose it. A couple of nights ago I ended up sobbing in the shower because I felt like I was failing at everything.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No… I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I get overwhelmed and cry, but I’ve never wanted to be gone or to do anything like that. I just want to feel better so I can be the mom my baby needs.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 25: Screening Summary – Postpartum Visit  
Date: [today’s date]  
Source: Patient self-report on 10-item EPDS-style questionnaire

I. Primary symptoms endorsed  
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness, anhedonia (daily crying, inability to laugh or anticipate pleasure)  
- Marked guilt/self-blame over routine infant-care events  
- Clinically significant anxiety: daily “no-reason” worry, panic spells with chest tightness, intrusive fears of infant harm  
- Sleep disturbance driven by ruminating and hypervigilance (difficulty initiating/maintaining sleep even when infant sleeps)  
- Feeling overwhelmed and “drowning” in daily tasks

II. Pattern consistency  
All mood, anxiety, and coping items are positive; enjoyment and self-esteem items are strongly negative. No evidence of hypomanic or psychotic features.

III. Areas of screening significance  
– Meets screening criteria for probable major depressive episode with peripartum onset (≥5 mood/cognitive/functional symptoms, onset ≤4 wk postpartum)  
– Co-occurring anxiety symptoms (possible perinatal anxiety disorder)  
– Impaired functioning in infant care and household tasks

IV. Risk factors noted  
✓ Depressed mood most of the day, nearly every day  
✓ Diminished interest/pleasure  
✓ Feelings of worthlessness, excessive guilt  
✓ Sleep disruption secondary to mood  
✓ Psychomotor/mental overwhelm  
✓ No suicidal ideation reported (explicitly denied)

V. Safety  
Patient denies thoughts of self-harm or harm to infant. No protective concerns identified at present; routine safety plan discussion recommended.

VI. Overall screening impression  
High likelihood of moderate-to-severe postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety; scores suggest referral for comprehensive diagnostic assessment and evidence-based treatment is warranted.
